taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station BMGS-bori-field, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1005 | 3.42 | 3.42
2 | 3588 | 6.33 | 9.76
3 | 1358 | 10.9 | 20.7
4 | 333 | 9.08 | 29.7
5 | 2950 | 36.8 | 66.5
6 | 5469 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as H-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station BMGS-bori-field, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report — BMGS-bori-field, Bori Metropolis**

The interpreted layer model shows six layers with resistivities (ohm-m) of 1005, 3588, 1358, 333, 2950, and 5469, corresponding to depths of base at 3.42, 9.76, 20.7, 29.7, and 66.5 m (layer 6 unbounded).

Applying the curve-type convention to each successive triplet of resistivities:
- Layers 1-2-3 (1005<3588>1358): K
- Layers 2-3-4 (3588>1358>333): Q
- Layers 3-4-5 (1358>333<2950): H
- Layers 4-5-6 (333<2950<5469): A

This yields a composite curve type of **KQHA**, not a simple single-letter type. The on-file classification of "H-type" does not match the computed sequence, as only one segment (layers 3-4-5) actually exhibits an H pattern. The full resistivity profile is more complex, alternating between K, Q, H, and A behavior across depth, and should be re-reviewed before finalizing the station classification.

{"curve_type_stated": "KQHA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
